title: Brothers, cousins and aunts and uncles in the Fraser family
summary: He names his other brothers, piano-playing cousins and his father's siblings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And you might tell about your other brothers, too. I know you're younger.

Yeah, well, I have another brother which died in 49. My name is Alec Fraser. He was a piano player. He started off... Dave Williams, the piano player now playing in the French quarters. And he started a cousin of mine who died, too, called Mitchell Fraser. That was my father's youngest brother, Michelle Fraser. He started him out of play. Then he made... He played a while. He died in 49, yeah. And Dave Williams' mother, which I know you know him, Dave. His mother is ours as two cousins.
He was in the band that you all had last year with Lawrence.

Lawrence went to Cincinnati, yeah. And... And... Let me see, that's a Fraser, too, because... His mother's father was my father's brother. His name was Rosamore John Fraser. Then... You want me to get in down to it when I first started playing? Yes. And then you can start...
How many brothers and sisters did your father have?

My father had two brothers, two sisters. Oh, two brothers and two sisters. Yeah, Michelle Fraser, John Fraser, and Catherine Fraser, and Jeanette Fraser. Jeanette Fraser was Lawrence and then my mother.
What was your father's name again?
Samson Franklin Fraser. Samson Franklin Fraser. And...
Was he the oldest of the family, or...?
No, he was the second oldest, my father. Rosamore John Fraser was the oldest brother. My father was the second oldest brother. And Michelle Fraser was the youngest brother.
And... That was a fellow by the name of Mitchell Fraser, another old-time piano player. He died... I'd say about... It's close to ten years now. And... And... Well, me and me... Amelia Bond...
Your younger brother, you still have another young...

Yeah, Simon Fraser. Yeah, he's living with my second oldest sister, yeah. Yeah. I think it's in the 26th... No, the 2500 Dumaine Street. He was in... That's the one... He allowed him how to play the piano to, Simon Fraser, yeah. And... Let's see, we have... Like I first said, I started... Now, my oldest brother, and Paul Barberin, another old drummer, they all started by Amarico's Woodyard on North Ramport Street years ago. And Sam, he played with Kid René and part with Louis Armstrong, before Louis ever think about leaving the Orleans to go north. See, they play with the old-time bands around, yeah. And he's the one... In fact, I used to use his drums around the front to him, you know, the practice behind the old-time... They call it the... These... Self-winding Victrola's. Oh, yeah. Yeah. Back around in 1920, like that, 1919. Right after World War I. But before that, like I said, I used to practice around the room on sticks, you know, just beating on steps and all like that. And then following behind the old-time pianola players, pianos. You see, I used to practice on that. Then I went along and started playing with this... That time before, radio time, we used to have...give house parties with piano and drum.
